title: History
tagline: Historians, court chroniclers and landmark documents, from the Book of Documents and Sima Qian to the Korean Declaration of Independence and the Constitution of Japan
hero_caption: Volumes of the Annals of the Joseon Dynasty from the Taebaeksan mountain archive
intro: East Asia has the longest continuous tradition of historical writing in the world. From the Zhou court scribes and Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian, China developed the official dynastic history, compiled by each dynasty for its predecessor, which Japan, Korea and Vietnam adapted for their own courts; alongside it grew private chronicles, interpretive histories, war diaries and the evidential scholarship of the Qing. This section gathers those histories together with the codes, edicts, treaties, declarations and constitutions that shaped the region, from the Tang Code to the Constitution of Japan. Manuscripts, early printed editions and original documents are shown from Wikimedia Commons; portraits are paintings or later imagined likenesses, never photographs.
